passage.title: 'The Man Behind the Plays', a teacher-written biography for TGA
paras: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564, the son of a glove-maker. At eighteen he married, and by his late twenties he was in London, writing and acting.
In 1599 his company opened the Globe, an open-air theatre on the south bank of the Thames. There, and later at the indoor Blackfriars, his plays drew crowds of every class.
When James I became king in 1603, the company became the King's Men. The Tempest, one of the last plays he wrote alone, was performed at court in 1611.
Shakespeare died in 1616. Seven years later, two friends collected his plays in the First Folio. Without their loyalty, half his plays might have been lost for ever.

panels.title: How a biography is built
points: Facts chosen to show what mattered

head: Not this
This
rows: A biography is only facts, so it has no viewpoint.
The writer chooses which facts to include and how to phrase them: 'drew crowds of every class' and 'Without their loyalty' show admiration.

keywords.def: a true account of a person's life written by someone else
the first sentence that sums up a paragraph
the writer's feeling towards the subject

questions.q: Retrieve: when did the Globe open, and where?
questions.a: 1599, on the south bank of the River Thames.

questions.q: What is the topic sentence of paragraph 3, and what does it sum up?
questions.a: 'When James I became king in 1603, the company became the King's Men': it sums up Shakespeare's link to the royal court.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, explain how the writer shows admiration for Shakespeare. Use two quotations. Starter: 'The writer admires Shakespeare, which is shown when...'
questions.a: Two embedded quotations (e.g. 'drew crowds of every class', 'Without their loyalty') with explanations of their effect.

questions.q: Extend: write a topic sentence for a new paragraph about The Tempest.
questions.a: For example: The Tempest is often read as Shakespeare's farewell to the stage.

questions.q: Stretch: what does the biography leave out, and why might that be?
questions.a: Little about his private life, because few records survive and the focus is his work.

questions.q: Why is the biography in chronological order?
options: So the reader can follow the life from birth to legacy
questions.a: B) So the reader can follow the life from birth to legacy. Biographies usually follow time order; C and A are wrong about form and purpose.
